The rationale text is here so a reader can audit the labels themselves, not just the system's agreement with them.
authored_by: Steven Pequeno (the labels) with personal-agent (proposed reasoning, reviewed and agreed 2026-10-11)

authored_against.note: The labels below were authored against this profile. The profile was later revised (see refrozen) and every label re-checked against the added class.

reason_classes.in_scope: the profile's core work: scoped advisory, discovery or implementation in cloud, IAM, data or AI
reason_classes.product_not_services: the issuer is buying a product or licences and the services are incidental
reason_classes.functional_stack_not_held: winning requires vendor-specific functional expertise the profile excludes (ERP or student systems, SAP/Oracle/Workday configuration, Dynamics functional work)
reason_classes.operations_not_projects: the work is continuous monitoring, service desk or managed operations rather than a project
reason_classes.geography: winning requires a recurring on-site presence the profile cannot commit to
reason_classes.not_qualified: a minimum track record, contract vehicle, credential or clearance makes the firm ineligible before capability is assessed — unreachable rather than unsuitable
reason_classes.staff_augmentation: the issuer is buying hours or bodies under a standing agreement rather than commissioning a delivered project

baseline_note: The title-only keyword baseline is expected to fail on at least three of these. u-maine-system and hacc both read as AI or software work by title and are product purchases; tahoe reads as a plain IT consulting engagement and is a geography no-bid. If the baseline does not fail there, the pipeline is adding nothing and that is the finding (adr/0003).

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: The University is seeking a vendor-hosted SaaS solution.
labels.rationale: The issuer is buying licences for a hosted platform, not commissioning work: a flat-rate or unlimited-usage licence is required, the solution must be multi-model, and it must pass Accessibility and IT Security gates including FERPA. A services practice cannot supply the product the award depends on.

labels.label: bid
labels.evidence: consulting services for the following as described in Section 3 – Scope of Services ... Cloud Migration Discovery and Strategic Services ... Identity & Access Management (IAM) strategy, and Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) strategy
labels.rationale: Pure advisory: discovery, strategy and target-state design in cloud, identity and zero trust, which is the profile's core. Three-year initial term with renewals, and evaluation is qualitative rather than price-dominated.
labels.counterargument: Requires travel to Indianapolis and out-of-state registration, both mechanical rather than disqualifying.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: A Cloud-based SaaS solution only (no on-prem or self-hosted alternatives). Vendors must provide fully managed hosting, updates, scaling, monitoring, and security.
labels.rationale: A records-management product procurement with implementation attached. The award turns on supplying and running the platform — hosting, updates, scaling, monitoring — which the profile excludes.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: Recommended Dynamics 365 applications and licensing (e.g. Sales, Customer Service, Marketing) ... Re-implementation or refactoring of existing customizations
labels.rationale: End-to-end Microsoft Dynamics functional migration: recommending D365 applications and licensing, configuring business requirements, Power Platform flows and security roles, then training and change management. The profile holds no functional D365 capability and no Microsoft partner status.
labels.counterargument: The same scope is heavy on data migration, integration architecture, IAM design and refactoring unsupported plugins, which is platform engineering. This was the closest call in the set and was agreed rather than obvious.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: retain a qualified consultant team ... to provide Information Technology Services and Management including on-site support
labels.rationale: A three-year operations retainer with three renewal options, providing ongoing IT services and management. The word consultant does not make it advisory: the shape is continuous service delivery, not a project with an end.
labels.counterargument: The profile does accept fractional retainers, up to about two days a week — but not a three-year operations commitment with on-site support.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: In case of an emergency, be on-site within four (4) hours ... plan on two (2) days per week for on-site support
labels.rationale: The cleanest no-bid in the set. Winning requires a standing on-site presence at South Lake Tahoe and Stateline, roughly 14 of 20 support hours per week on site, plus a four-hour emergency on-site response and attendance at board meetings. Geography is a hard constraint, not a scoring penalty.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: experience and ability to provide Enterprise Resource Planning
labels.rationale: A 64-page procure-to-award for an ERP and student information system, with selection resting on demonstrated ERP implementation experience and total cost. Functional ERP and student-systems delivery is explicitly outside the profile.
labels.counterargument: Large, well funded and multi-year — attractive on money alone, which is the trap the profile exists to catch.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: 24x7x365 monitoring of denoted servers and critical network components ... Full-service desk ... Less than 4-hour response time for server down emergencies
labels.rationale: A managed-service retainer for a small city: round-the-clock monitoring, a service desk, an operations centre, and SQL Server, Laserfiche and Hyper-V administration. Three-year term with predictable revenue, and still an operations business the profile excludes.

labels.label: bid
labels.evidence: soliciting proposals from qualified consultant firms to develop a Six-Year Information Technology Strategic Plan
labels.rationale: A pure advisory deliverable — a six-year IT strategic plan for a city with about 60 users — with no on-site, licence, monitoring or hosting requirement anywhere in the text. Small in value, squarely in scope.
labels.counterargument: The contract is small enough that declining it would be a policy choice about revenue, not a capability judgement.

labels.label: bid
labels.evidence: Design and build the data commons website and backend infrastructure ... Implement metadata management, cataloging, and discovery tools (e.g., CKAN, Dataverse) ... AI Fairness and Bias Framework
labels.rationale: An implementation project in the profile's exact lane: platform build, metadata and API design, synthetic data tooling, and a fairness and bias framework with audit dashboards, plus governance, training and launch. Remote-friendly, with travel reimbursed at the standard mileage rate.

labels.label: bid
labels.evidence: The engagement will include advisory, implementation, and knowledge transfer components.
labels.rationale: AI integration, a Microsoft Fabric migration, a Dynamics 365 migration for a 211 call centre and an intelligent virtual assistant, specified as projects with deliverables and a one-year term. The work is squarely in scope even though the title says only consultant.
labels.counterargument: The summary line reads as staff augmentation — act as an extension of our Information Systems team, on an as-needed basis — which the profile excludes. Agreed as a bid: the deliverables are project-shaped, so this is the label with the least margin in the set.

labels.label: bid
labels.evidence: The Scope of Services for the UTMP includes a comprehensive review of IRCDUS's existing business processes
labels.rationale: An assessment engagement producing a technology master plan, plus vendor-neutral CIS selection support. Deliverables and phases rather than staffing, no on-site requirement, and the experience language is a scored demonstration rather than a minimum. The closest call is whether CIS selection support drifts into functional configuration of a customer information system; it does not — the work is evaluating vendor solutions, not configuring one.

labels.label: bid
labels.evidence: The purpose of this RFP is to procure comprehensive data warehousing services from a single vendor
labels.rationale: Explicitly a services procurement with a scope, deliverables and milestone-based pricing. The experience line asks for 'at least three (3) comparable engagements, preferably for public school districts' — 'preferably' makes it scored, not a gate, which is what keeps it out of the fifth class and in scope.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: Enterprise Data Warehouse and Performance Management Software and Related Items
labels.rationale: Two independent reasons. It is a software purchase — the title says so — and it is gated: a minimum of five years of K-12 data warehouse solutions, at least five successful Texas K-12 implementations, existing Texas references from similarly sized districts. The gate is primary because the firm is ineligible before capability is assessed. Partnering with a K-12-experienced sub would not fix the software gap, so the no-bid does not depend on which reading is taken.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.rationale: 'Pre-delivered' is the decisive word: the analytics exist before the contract, so the issuer is buying a platform rather than commissioning one. The counterargument, and the weakest call in this round: the document also asks for 'the proposed solution and implementation approach', and a platform procurement with a build phase is a services engagement wearing a product's name. Reviewed and agreed as a product purchase on 2026-10-11.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.rationale: The College's own cover sheet calls this 'RFP 05-2024 AI Software', the requirements score software access through the LMS, and the contract terms are licence terms. Buying AI tooling with services attached, not commissioning AI engineering — the award depends on supplying a product the firm does not have.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.evidence: MASTER AGREEMENTS FOR TECHNICAL STAFF AUGMENTATION SERVICES
labels.rationale: The title is the finding. Up to sixteen master agreements awarded to 'technical staff augmentation staffing agencies', two years plus three one-year options, with work issued as Work Orders on an as-needed basis. The firm does not do staff augmentation, and a five-year standing agreement is not a project with an end. This fixture is why the sixth class exists: as continuous_operations the reason text said 'continuous operations' about a document whose own words are 'staff augmentation'.

labels.label: no_bid
labels.rationale: A monthly managed-service contract with priced on-site labour — monthly managed services, hourly on-site support, emergency after-hours support — in Bristol Bay, Alaska. Two exclusions match: a recurring on-site presence outside DFW, and continuous operations rather than a project. 'Remote and on-site' describes the service, not an option; the profile treats geography as a hard constraint rather than a scoring penalty.
